newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Thursday on an unclear market trend partly due to recent directives from Beijing urging more strict supervision of futures trading, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,050 yuan ($2,415) per tonne, down 110 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 19,950 and hit a high of 20,110.
October rose 80 to 20,430 yuan, November 10 to 20,200, December unchanged at 20,150. February fell 90 to 20,050 and March 40 to 20,140.
Combined volume fell to 22,240 tonnes from 49,240.
Copper contracts opened mostly at their intra-day lows and short-covering pushed later-maturing contracts above the key 20,000-yuan support level.
Traders said investors were sidelined due to the reports of further futures trading restrictions, uncertainties on the London Metal Exchange and a holiday atmosphere.
In recent days, the securities authorities have issued two major documents on the need to control over-speculation and other problems in the futures markets.
"It made many investors cautious when they want to build new positions," one trader said.
